smooth adjective

not rough

also smooth to the touch, smoother

classical

Cic. N.D. 1.66: corpuscula quaedam lēvia, alia aspera (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ep. 115.8

lēvis, lēve

adjective, third declension

Smooth to the touch and to the eye, the opposite of asper. Not to be confused with levis, “light”, with a short e: Comenius sets the two side by side (below). Making something smooth is lēvigāre (see iron).

Other words

  • glaber, glabra, glabrum — hairless, smooth (of skin); bald

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Trin. 2.4.140; Varr. RR 2.2.6 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • illōs repertī in lītore calculī lēvēs et aliquid habentēs varietātis dēlectant

    smooth pebbles found on the beach, with a bit of colour in them, delight themSen. Ep. 115.8

  • Manus dīgnōscit tangendō … calidum et frīgidum, ūmidum et siccum, dūrum et molle, lēve et asperum, grave et leve.

    The hand tells by touch … hot and cold, wet and dry, hard and soft, smooth and rough, heavy and light.Comen. OP 41

See also soft, hard, iron.
